overview.summary: Cinematographers, also called directors of photography, are responsible for how a film or video looks, choosing camera, lighting and framing to tell the story visually.
overview.problems: They turn the director's vision into images that create the right mood and clarity.
overview.worksWith: Directors, camera operators, lighting crews, production designers and editors.
overview.workplaces: Film and TV sets, studios and locations, and increasingly commercials, music videos and online content.

timeline.title: Planning shots
timeline.description: The cinematographer reads the script, talks with the director and plans the look, lenses and lighting.
timeline.why: Planning avoids costly changes on set.

timeline.title: Setting up
timeline.description: The cinematographer plans camera positions and lighting with the crew.
timeline.why: A well-run set saves time and money.

timeline.title: Lighting the scene
timeline.description: The cinematographer shapes light and shadow to create mood.
timeline.why: Light is one of the most powerful storytelling tools.

timeline.title: Filming
timeline.description: The cinematographer directs the camera team, checks framing and focus and repeats takes.
timeline.why: Every take has to look right as well as work for the story.

timeline.title: Solving problems
timeline.description: Weather, time and equipment problems need quick decisions.
timeline.why: Few shoots go exactly to plan.

timeline.title: Checking the look
timeline.description: The cinematographer works with editors and colour specialists to finish the images.
timeline.why: The final look is shaped in post-production too.

responsibilities: Leading the camera and lighting crews
Reviewing and finishing the look in post-production
challenges: Days on set are long, often 12 hours or more.
The work is physical, with carrying equipment and working outdoors in all weather.
Work is project-based and income is uneven.
Competition is strong and the climb from assistant roles is long.
Many people's opinions have to be balanced.
workEnvironment: Film sets and locations, indoors and outdoors, in all weather, with long and irregular hours. Work is project-based and can involve travel. Some cinematographers work in studios or on commercials and online content.
rewards: A mix of art and technology
tradeoffs: Pay and opportunities that vary by country and industry

activity.title: Shoot a five-shot sequence with window light
steps: Choose a simple action, such as a person opening a door and sitting down.
Plan five shots, such as wide, medium, close-up, detail and over-the-shoulder.
Film them with a phone near a window, with friends who agree to take part.
Compare how light from the window changes the mood when the subject faces it or has their back to it.
Edit the shots together and ask what viewers noticed.
activity.outcome: You practise framing, lighting and planning shots for a story.
activity.safety: Film only in safe places with permission, do not film strangers, do not walk while looking at the screen, and avoid climbing or standing on furniture.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
